text:
sam: Heads-up — cluster syncs are piling up and GPU deploys are timing out. noticed a big argocd reconcile backlog after the midnight rollout.
ana: ugh, saw that. pods in gpu-pool kept in Pending because PVCs are stuck Terminating. kube finalizer on the PV? :eyes:
kevin: I grabbed logs from argocd-server, looks like we’re hitting sync-throttle + too many deletes in the app-of-apps root. argocd is queuing deletes and not pruning fast enough.
infra-bot: [alert] argocd_app_reconcile_duration_seconds spike on cluster-prod-eu
li: paste of `kubectl get pvc -n gpu-pool --show-finalizers` output:
```
NAME                 STATUS        VOLUME        FINALIZERS
gpu-claim-01         Terminating   pvc-abcdef    [kubernetes.io/pvc-protection]
gpu-claim-02         Bound         pvc-111111    []
```
kevin: that pvc-protection finalizer prevents PV deletion -> app deletion waits -> argocd prune queue grows -> sync thrashes.
sam: also seeing a ton of 429s from GitHub in controller logs, so appset+app-of-apps controllers are retrying slowly. combined backpressure.
ana: so root cause triangle: 1) orphaned PVC finalizers, 2) argocd sync throttling behavior for mass deletions, 3) git API rate limits.
li: suggestion: unblock by forcibly removing pvc finalizers for those stuck claims in gpu namespace after ensuring no data needed.
kevin: steps I propose:
1) pause the app-of-apps root (set spec.syncPolicy.automated=false) for 10m
2) run `kubectl patch pvc gpu-claim-01 -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}' --type=merge` (after backup check)
3) resume automation and watch argocd prune queue
sam: +1 but add a canary: restart one GPU node first and drain it to ensure there are no underlying kubelet issues causing PVC not to detach.
ana: I can take step 2 and watch infra metrics. I'll wait for a thumbs-up from security on forcing finalizer removal (we have a small window where customer job might still own the disk).
infra-bot: [info] creating incident stub: INC-2026-045 (argocd-sync-backpressure)
kevin: also let's reduce concurrency for AppSet controller temporarily to avoid hammering GitHub — patch controller config to set --concurrent=5
li: FYI, I ran `kubectl get events -n argocd` and saw repeated errors:
```
Warning  ReconcileError  3m   argocd-operator  timed out waiting for application "apps/gpu-deploy" to be deleted
```
sam: after unblocking PVCs, we should implement a policy: app-of-apps should set cascade deletion to foreground with pre-delete hook that removes PV reclaim policy to Retain? or vice versa — we discussed using Retain when we want to avoid stuck volumes. need doc.
ana: I'll open a short RFC for deleting strategy for GPU stateful workloads and add a runbook for forced finalizer removal.
kevin: also we should add monitoring alert for sustained argocd prune queue length > 50 for >5m. right now only reconcile failure alerts exist.
li: quick action plan for the next hour:
- sam: drain + restart one node (start in 5m)
- nana: prepare finalizer removal and contact security
- kevin: patch appset concurrency + pause root app
- li: watch argocd metrics and GitHub rate limits
sam: doing node drain now, will post progress.
nana: (typo) oop meant nana: will hold until security OK.
kevin: once cleared, run a small automation to delete 10 stuck PVCs and verify argocd queue drains.
sam: update: node drained, no kubelet errors, PVCs still Terminating. proceeding with finalizer removal on the 2 oldest ones.
li: confirm, argocd prune queue length dropped from 214 -> 18 after manual finalizer removals and resuming automation. :tada:
kevin: great. followups: RFC + runbook + patch AppSet controller concurrency + alert rule. I'll create tickets.
nana: thanks team. logging postmortem draft in #incidents once we stabilize.
infra-bot: [resolved] INC-2026-045 closed (mitigated)
